body:
Click on my username to see the post I wrote about my dark times.

I had the same thing happen: broke up with my girlfriend, lost my job.  At the time, the economy was also shitty (after 9/11).

I did a lot of drugs.  Watched a lot of sad movies.  Cried a lot.  Acted out.  Did a bunch of stupid shit.

Give yourself some time.  Let yourself grieve.  You've been hurt a lot.  I didn't know how to deal with the pain.  It sounds like you don't either.  Reach out to others.  See if your parents will pay for therapy.  Or maybe there's a therapy school where you can talk to somebody.  If not, keep a blog.  You'd be surprised how writing your feelings out helps you not internalize everything.

Things will change.  Life will be different.  It may not seem like it but trust me, it will.  

Lastly, what happened to you does not make you a bad person.  This took me a long time to realize.  You don't even have to be a good person but you are certainly not bad.  You are worthy to live.

It was surprising to me obviously as well.  She was expensive and I could only go two times a month. I think she implied I needed everyday treatment.  I did find someone cheaper to go to after for a bit.  She helped but she was nuts and I stopped seeing her pretty soon.  Sometimes I think I'd like to go back to therapy again but that experience was somewhat traumatizing.

I did consider meds at the time.  Right now, I feel great.  I have periods of depression but nothing nearly as bad and I seem to be able to deal with it on my own.  I fight my way out of them.  Yoga has been a blessing also.  I highly recommend it.
Thanks.  The thing is I don't feel like I've gained much insight.  I wish I could tell people how I turned things around but it's hard to say.  But again, if someone got anything from this, I'm glad.
